# Thirza Abernethy

## Overview

- **Age:** Eighty-five years old  <sub>[v5 c2 P6](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0006)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c1 P13](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0013)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive  <sub>[v5 c2 P6](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0006), [v5 c3 P6](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0006)</sub>
- **Origin:** Brierley  <sub>[v1 c8 P11](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0011)</sub>
- **Role:** Cook and housekeeper  <sub>[v1 c16 P27](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0027)</sub>

## Appearance

Thirza Abernethy is a tall, slender woman with sharp angles and a pale face. In her younger years, her dark hair had graying strands bound back tightly in a firm bun fastened with hairpins, which eventually turned silvered and then snow-white in her old age. She has rough, labor-calloused hands and lined cheeks, and her eyesight suffered a severe decline before stabilizing and later unexpectedly improving in her eighties.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P13](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0013), [v1 c33 P15](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0015), [v2 c8 P3](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0003), [v2 c12 P39](../source/v02-c12.md#nw-v02-c12-p0039), [v2 c14 P4](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0004), [v2 c15 P43](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0043), [v4 c34 P1](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0001), [v5 c2 P6](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0006)_

## Personality

Thirza is a stern, practical, and highly disciplined woman who maintains a clean household and values hard work, thrifty habits, and good morals. She is composed, rational, and somewhat rigid, often attached to teaching moral lessons to children and reserved about expressing affection. Beneath her strict exterior lies a strong commitment to duty, deep loyalty to her family, a quiet sense of humor, and a heart that grows significantly softer, kinder, and more mellow over time.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P8](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0008), [v1 c1 P13](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0013), [v1 c5 P12](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0012), [v1 c7 P19](../source/v01-c07.md#nw-v01-c07-p0019), [v1 c8 P41](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0041), [v1 c22 P3](../source/v01-c22.md#nw-v01-c22-p0003), [v1 c23 P25](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0025), [v1 c27 P3](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0003), [v1 c30 P3](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0003), [v1 c37 P20](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0020), [v1 c38 P46](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0046), [v2 c7 P31](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0031), [v3 c22 P2](../source/v03-c22.md#nw-v03-c22-p0002)_

## History

Thirza Abernethy lived at Grey Shutters in Brierley with her brother Obed. Expecting to adopt an orphan boy to assist on the farm, they were mistakenly sent an orphan girl, Nell Harcourt. Although initially planning to return her, Thirza decided to keep and raise Nell, developing a deep, protective affection for her despite maintaining a strict and moralizing discipline. Over the years, Thirza raised Nell into adulthood, supported her education, and eventually coped with the sudden loss of Obed to a heart condition. Following Mary Farrow's death, Thirza also welcomed the orphans Robin and Lucy into her household. Later in life, she suffered from failing vision, though specialists halted the loss of her sight, which eventually improved in her advanced years. She celebrated Nell's marriage to Hugh Carrow, traveled to Seven Gulls to support Nell during the birth of her family, and lived to an advanced age of eighty-five at Grey Shutters, warmly welcoming Nell's visiting children.

_Sources: [v1 c6 P3](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0003), [v1 c6 P29](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0029), [v1 c12 P46](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0046), [v1 c30 P16](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0016), [v1 c37 P1](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0001), [v1 c37 P20](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0020), [v2 c1 P29](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0029), [v2 c14 P4](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0004), [v2 c18 P11](../source/v02-c18.md#nw-v02-c18-p0011), [v4 c1 P5](../source/v04-c01.md#nw-v04-c01-p0005), [v4 c15 P1](../source/v04-c15.md#nw-v04-c15-p0001), [v4 c19 P0](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0000), [v5 c2 P6](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0006), [v5 c3 P6](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0006)_

## Background by volume

- Inherited a prized oval amethyst brooch containing a lock of her mother's hair  <sub>[v1 c13 P20](../source/v01-c13.md#nw-v01-c13-p0020)</sub>
- Was close friends in her youth with John Carrow, whom people called her beau  <sub>[v1 c37 P37](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0037)</sub>
- Recalled being called a 'dark, homely little thing' by her aunt during childhood  <sub>[v1 c9 P44](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0044)</sub>
- Moved into Grey Shutters upon reaching adulthood and resided there for decades  <sub>[v1 c1 P31](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0031), [v2 c17 P73](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0073), [v3 c22 P3](../source/v03-c22.md#nw-v03-c22-p0003)</sub>
- Raised under her father's view that children should not enter school before age seven  <sub>[v2 c10 P86](../source/v02-c10.md#nw-v02-c10-p0086)</sub>
- Lost her longtime Frost Maiden tree in a severe March gale  <sub>[v3 c39 P10](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0010)</sub>
- Had never traveled as far as sixty miles from home prior to visiting Seven Gulls  <sub>[v4 c15 P1](../source/v04-c15.md#nw-v04-c15-p0001)</sub>

## Quotes

> Provided you are mindful to address me with deference, I suppose doing so will not be rude. With the exception of the clergyman, every person in Brierley, regardless of age, refers to me as Thirza. On occasions when it occurs to him, he says Miss Abernethy.  <sub>[v1 c8 P11](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0011)</sub>

> As long as Obed and I remain here, Grey Shutters will always be a home for you, yet no one can tell what the future holds in this unpredictable life, so being ready for anything is wise.  <sub>[v1 c30 P16](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0016)</sub>

> Nell, we still have one another. If you were not with me—had you never arrived—I cannot imagine what my plight would be. Oh, Nell, perhaps I have been somewhat stern and severe toward you, as I am well aware—yet despite that, you must never believe my love for you was any less than Obed's.  <sub>[v1 c37 P20](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0020)</sub>

> Sixty years I’ve resided in this place, and not once have I gone out on the pond.  <sub>[v2 c17 P73](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0073)</sub>

> I can only be glad that Nell did not die  <sub>[v4 c19 P26](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0026)</sub>
